architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: The three controlled preparations must have a max/min realized-viscosity spread below 1.50x at each matched temperature in the 80-130 C sweep.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: The state-control objective is falsified if the controlled preparations have a max/min spread greater than 2.80x at any matched temperature, because this fails to beat the documented lower bound of the uncontrolled E2 spread. A spread from 1.50x through 2.80x is inconclusive for the stated control objective and does not falsify H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the matched 120 C thermal-hold comparison only with randomized, fully recorded preparation histories, at least three independent preparations per formulation, and explicit stratification or adjustment for the realized viscosity-scale coordinate before interpreting formulation differences.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Between-preparation max/min spread of the realized viscosity-scale coordinate a_fr at matched temperature across three controlled preparations.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C02 is the centered E2 reactive-core anchor, and M-REPEAT directly addresses the documented realization-state uncertainty that can confound all later drift comparisons. It does not test the modifier hypotheses; it establishes whether the process state is controlled well enough for those tests to be interpretable.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic's high-severity objection and the robustness concern over the Proposer's M-HOLD recommendation. The proposer selected a direct drift measurement, but its intervention-free formulation cannot falsify or discriminate any registered modifier hypothesis and leaves substantial process-state confounding. M-REPEAT is therefore selected as a state-control experiment before interpreting subsequent hold comparisons.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with unresolved dependence on modifier chemistry versus reactive-core dilution.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: Original 120 C thermal holds show SI_15_60 of 51.54% for E5 versus 9.51% for E1 over the measured 15-60 minute window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local temperature sweeps resolve a monotonic temperature response over 80-130 C, and the original E1/E5 holds resolve drift over 15-90 minutes, but the realized viscosity scale is poorly controlled: E2 shows three-run max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C with CV values of approximately 0.46-0.58. Viscosity units are also unreported, so absolute level cannot be inferred.
measurement_requirements: Measure at least two independent preparations for each candidate using a matched 120 C hold with observations at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes, and report SI_15_60 directly.
Match or explicitly record reactive mass fraction, preparation history, temperature, and measurement conditions so drift can be compared with the E1-based linear-dilution prediction.
Include an acrylic-only composition and a composition with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction at comparable reactive mass fraction to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
Measure the 80-130 C viscosity sweep for repeated preparations or otherwise quantify the realized viscosity-scale displacement before interpreting drift differences as formulation effects.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and process state, does a resin-modified composition suppress 120 C isothermal viscosity drift substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, and is low drift obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is nonzero rather than with acrylic-like modification alone?

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 4.75% across at least two repeats, the registered card criterion accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE and would also falsify H-DUAL because low drift occurred without either modifier axis. However, because this is an unmodified control, the result does not establish resin-specific suppression mechanistically.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 9.51%, H-RESIN is falsified for this comparison and the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction remains compatible with the observation. H-CORE is falsified only if drift is below 4.75%.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 4.75% and 9.51%, or a result unresolved within the 2.00% measurement resolution, would not separate the registered hypotheses; it would indicate that the control establishes neither strong suppression nor a decisive linear-dilution baseline.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has the same deterministic component vector, but its reactive-core composition departs from the centered E2 anchor without adding any hypothesis-discriminating intervention.

It has the same deterministic component vector, but its altered reactive-core balance adds a stoichiometric/composition perturbation that complicates interpretation without separating H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.

It directly assesses realization-state spread and reduces process-state uncertainty, but its primary observable is the viscosity-scale coordinate rather than the thermal-hold drift coordinate on which the hypotheses disagree.

proposer.reasoning: The direct 120 C matched-window hold is preferable to model-based sweep or anchor measurements for the declared failure mode. Among the genuinely tied top cards, S1C02 is scientifically preferable because it is the local E2 reactive-core anchor and therefore supplies the cleanest baseline for later modifier comparisons. Its limitation is decisive: it separates none of the registered hypothesis pairs, so a subsequent acrylic-only and minor-tackifier-containing intervention would still be required.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C02 is the centered E2 reactive-core anchor, preserving the characterized MDI/PDP70/PPG2000 proportions and avoiding the additional stoichiometric or composition perturbations present in the other tied cards. The matched-window hold is directly interpretable, but this no-intervention control cannot discriminate the modifier hypotheses by itself.

robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal is inside the deterministic tied top set, although the policy order lists S1C01 first. Selecting S1C02 is justified by scientific evidence: it is the centered E2 reactive-core anchor and provides the cleanest baseline for later matched modifier comparisons, rather than being a preference unsupported by the data.
residual_decision_risk: The supplied stability sweep is withheld, so weight-perturbation robustness and recommendation-flip boundaries are unavailable.
S1C02 does not separate H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL and cannot support modifier-specific causal claims by itself.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state; six process fields are missing and the documented E2 realized-viscosity spread may confound comparisons.
At least two repeats are specified, but the threshold rule does not define whether acceptance applies to each repeat, the mean, or another prespecified summary.
A result near the decision thresholds may remain unresolved within the declared 2.00% measurement resolution.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not invalidate the value of running S1C02 as an E2 reactive-core control, and the skeptic explicitly recommends retaining it. It does invalidate the proposed outcome interpretation: because S1C02 contains neither acrylic-like modifier nor minor tackifier-like modifier, all three registered hypotheses predict the same 9.51% drift there. Its result cannot falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL, establish resin-specific suppression, or test tackifier necessity. The control should be run in a controlled preparation block alongside an acrylic-only composition and a nonzero-minor-tackifier composition, with a prespecified repeat-summary rule and recorded process-state fields.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The supplied payload withholds top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary, so the fraction of stable re-weightings, VOI gap, and per-term flip boundaries cannot be assessed. The available deterministic ranking shows S1C01 through S1C09 M-HOLD-120 cards tied at the top, with S1C02 tied with the policy-first S1C01. Any change among these tied cards is therefore not shown to require a weight perturbation. No defensible perturbation-based change to S1C02 can be identified from the supplied report.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: SI_15_60 can be directly measured with the specified 15, 30, 45, and 60 minute protocol, and the 4.75% threshold is numerically separated from the 9.51% reference by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. However, the registered falsification criteria are intervention-specific. S1C02 contains no resin, so an at-or-above-9.51% result cannot falsify H-RESIN, and it is not the registered acrylic-only composition required for the stated H-DUAL test. The protocol can measure the control outcome, but it cannot meet the claimed causal falsification criteria.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that the experiment discriminates reactive-core dilution from resin-specific suppression or establishes tackifier necessity would be unsupported; the experiment supplies only a baseline control for a later comparison.
objections.objection: The selected S1C02::M-HOLD-120 formulation is the unmodified E2 reactive-core control: AC1920 = 0.0%, TK100 = 0.0%, and reactive_mass_fraction = 1.0. Consequently, the measured SI_15_60 value is predicted as 9.51% by H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL alike, as explicitly shown in hypothesis_discrimination_detail. No registered hypothesis pair is separated. In particular, this experiment contains neither the acrylic-only composition nor the nonzero-minor-tackifier composition required to test H-DUAL, and it contains no resin-modified composition on which to test H-RESIN's suppression prediction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could be used to claim falsification of H-DUAL even though the specific registered acrylic-only contrast was never measured.
objections.objection: The proposer correctly declares H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL in hypotheses_not_separated, but the outcome_interpretation still assigns falsification roles that do not match the registered interventions. The criterion that an acrylic-only composition reaching low drift falsifies H-DUAL cannot be applied to S1C02, because S1C02 has neither acrylic-like modifier nor minor tackifier. A no-modifier result is not the registered acrylic-only test.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Differences observed in any later comparison could be attributed to modifier chemistry only after controlling realization state; this experiment does not provide that control and cannot support axis-specific attribution.
objections.objection: There is no simultaneous movement of the two modifier axes in S1C02, so the composition itself is not confounded by acrylic and tackifier changes. However, both axes are fixed at zero, making all modifier-mechanism attributions unavailable. The experiment cannot distinguish acrylic effects from tackifier effects, test whether either axis suppresses drift, or determine whether the reactive-core baseline differs from a matched resin-modified composition. The process_state_risk_detail also reports that M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, with base_before_measurement_plan = 0.75 and six missing process fields.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be reported as falsifying H-RESIN or H-DUAL even though the causal intervention specified by each hypothesis was absent.
objections.objection: The stated criterion 'H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above 9.51%' is not logically testable on S1C02, because 9.51% is the H-CORE linear-dilution reference for the unmodified E2 core, not an observation from a resin-modified composition. A control result at or above 9.51% can show that this unmodified control did not exhibit strong suppression, but it cannot falsify the claim that resin modification produces superlinear suppression. Likewise, the H-DUAL criterion is not operationally applicable because the measured composition is neither acrylic-only nor tackifier-containing.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result near 4.75% or 9.51% could be classified inconsistently, weakening any claimed falsification even for the baseline behavior.
objections.objection: The numerical low-drift threshold of 4.75% is 4.76 percentage points below the 9.51% linear prediction and therefore exceeds the declared 2.00% resolution, so the threshold itself is not too close to the stated resolution. However, the protocol specifies only 'at least two independent repeats' and does not define whether the criterion applies to every repeat, the mean, or a confidence interval. Given the documented uncontrolled E2 viscosity-scale spread of 2.80-3.57x at 80-130 C and M-HOLD-120's lack of process-state control, the protocol does not specify a reproducible decision rule for borderline repeat results.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No major interpretability problem follows; the weakness is experimental discrimination, not the definition of SI_15_60 itself.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly computed from the matched 15 and 60 minute viscosity measurements under M-HOLD-120. Unlike M-SWEEP's fitted E_eta or M-ANCHOR's model-conditioned reconstruction, it requires no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. The observable is therefore interpretable for the stated 120 C hold, although its causal interpretation remains limited by the absent interventions and uncontrolled process state.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain S1C02 as an E2 reactive-core control, but run it in the same controlled preparation block as at least one acrylic-only composition and one composition with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction, matched on reactive mass fraction and process history. Use the same M-HOLD-120 protocol with at least two independent preparations per composition, define whether thresholds apply to each repeat or a prespecified summary, and record or control the process-state fields identified as missing. This design would directly test H-CORE versus H-RESIN and the acrylic-only versus tackifier-containing contrast required for H-DUAL.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02 is an unmodified reactive-core control for which H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL all predict the same 9.51% drift, so the stated thresholds cannot logically falsify the resin-modification or dual-axis hypotheses without measuring the corresponding modifier interventions.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

result.limitation: Not a resin-modifier study and not a hold-stability experiment.

result.agent_hint: A peer-reviewed PUR study reported 15% acrylic resin as the overall preferred addition level in its system; this independently supports 15% as a coarse acrylic-axis candidate level.
result.limitation: Optimization target was overall high-temperature adhesive performance, not thermal-hold viscosity; chemistry differs from the local system.
result.pattern: polyether polyol + polyphenylene-ether polyol + acrylic resin + crystalline polyester polyol + MDI

result.agent_hint: A 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer formulation showed substantially slower viscosity rise than the equal-loading higher-OH acrylic comparator; this supports both a 25% acrylic candidate level and the hypothesis that lower reactive-group density can improve hot-hold stability.
result.limitation: Different acrylic chemistry and much longer hold window; does not establish the local mechanism.
result.pattern: PPG1000 + PPG2000 + polyester polyol + low-OH acrylic copolymer + MDI

result.agent_hint: At the same 25 wt% acrylic loading, the higher-OH acrylic analogue exhibited roughly twice the reported 8 h viscosity increase of the low-OH example, making modifier functionality a plausible stability variable rather than loading alone.
result.limitation: Patent comparison; acrylic materials are not AC1920 and the result is not a direct local-system measurement.
result.pattern: same formulation as Example 10 but higher-OH acrylic copolymer

result.agent_hint: A functional-tackifier-containing formulation had lower reported stability rise than the no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator in the same example set, supporting the idea that modifier identity can change hot-melt stability.
result.limitation: Other formulation variables including MDI differ; not an isolated causal comparison.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + functional tackifier + MDI

result.agent_hint: The no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator reported a larger stability value than several modifier-containing examples, providing directional support for a modifier-family hypothesis rather than proof of one optimum.
result.limitation: MDI and other variables differ across the table; use only as directional evidence.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + MDI; no acrylic polymer or functional tackifier

result.agent_hint: The patent states that tackifiers and rheology-control agents may be used in small amounts, typically below about 10 wt%, supporting 10% as a conservative upper coarse level for the minor-tackifier axis.
result.limitation: No specific thermal-hold comparison and no exact match to TK100.
result.pattern: polyurethane hot melt with optional tackifiers/plasticizers/rheology-control agents

result.agent_hint: Published formulation art explicitly treats viscosity rise during prolonged hot holding as a design failure mode and cites a preferred stability level of no more than about 25% increase over 4-10 h; this supports thermal-hold stability as an independent design objective.
result.limitation: The time scale is much longer than the local 15-60 min test and should not be converted into a local numerical threshold.
result.pattern: thermally stable reactive hot melt urethane composition
